extracted.intended_audience: registered patent attorneys, respondents in USPTO disciplinary proceedings, and Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedure and standards for imposing reciprocal discipline (public reprimand) by the USPTO based on a state bar's public reprimand, including service requirements, opportunity to respond, and the consequences of failing to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h) predicated upon receiving a public reprimand by a duly constituted authority of a State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "This notice concerns Derek R. Van Gilder ... who is a registered patent attorney ... has been reprimanded for violating 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h), predicated upon receiving a public reprimand by a duly constituted authority of a State."

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline process under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the state authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office filed a "Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline Pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24" requesting imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by the Evidentiary Panel for State Bar District No. 8-7 of the State Bar of Texas in Commission for Lawyer Discipline v. Derek Robert Van Gilder, No. 201504822.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and notice requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and Order must be served on the respondent (here attempted by certified first-class mail with tracking); delivery attempts and receipt evidence are part of the service record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the file: first attempt sent by certified first-class mail (receipt no. 70160910000045132047) remained 'In Transit' per USPS tracking and was not returned; a second certified mailing (receipt no. 70160910000045132078) was delivered on June 23, 2017. The Notice and Order notified Respondent of the Complaint and response rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to oppose under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent is afforded an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice and Order provided Respondent 40 days to file a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state discipline, based on reasons enumerated in the regulation; Respondent did not file a response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond — no genuine issue of material fact
rubrics_metrics.description: If the respondent fails to file a response, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), permitting imposition of reciprocal discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "In light of Respondent's failure to file a response, it is hereby determined that there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and public reprimand of Respondent is the appropriate discipline."

rubrics_metrics.name: Form of reciprocal discipline — public reprimand identical to state sanction
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate under the regulation, the Director may order reciprocal discipline identical to the discipline imposed by the state authority — here, a public reprimand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order language: "Respondent be, and hereby is, reprimanded; The OED Director publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette." The discipline imposed mirrors the state judgment of Public Reprimand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to publish and comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must publish the Notice of reprimand in the Official Gazette and otherwise comply with the procedural publication requirements set forth in 37 C.F.R. § 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: "The OED Director publish the following Notice in the Official Gazette" and "The OED Director comply with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59."

rubrics_metrics.name: Underlying misconduct standard — conflict of interest (Texas Rule 1.06(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: State disciplinary finding that the lawyer violated Rule 1.06(b)(2) (Texas Disciplinary Rules of Professional Conduct) by representing a person while also representing that person's company and taking actions that reasonably appeared to be or became adversely limited by duties to another client or the lawyer's own interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted rule language: the rule "forbids a lawyer from representing a person if such representation, inter alia, reasonably appears to be or become adversely limited by the lawyer's responsibilities to another client, or to a third person, or by the lawyer's own interests." Factual findings include drafting trust amendments that reduced a child's distribution, appointing Respondent co-trustee and successor trustee, executing new power of attorney naming Respondent attorney-in-fact, and a subsequent medical diagnosis of dementia for the client.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary action is taken pursuant to federal statute and USPTO regulations, namely 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Order states: "This action is taken pursuant to the provisions of 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24." It also notes where disciplinary decisions are made available for public review (OED FOIA Reading Room).
